A new attack technique known as TrustSink allows hackers with privileged access to register a rogue external multi-factor authentication (MFA) provider, enabling them to capture user passwords during legitimate login attempts. This attack takes advantage of Microsoft's Entra system, redirecting users to a fake password prompt while appearing to complete the authentication process normally. Security researchers warn that once the rogue provider is established, it can remain in the authentication flow, capturing subsequent password changes.

 - The TrustSink attack exploits the trust placed in external MFA providers to steal user credentials.
 - The attack requires an already compromised privileged account to register a malicious authentication method.

Source: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/rogue-external-mfa-providers-can-steal-passwords-during-logins/

Small Language Models (SLMs) with fewer than 3 billion parameters show limitations in their ability to generate confidence signals based on token-level entropy, which is ineffective in 91% of cases. However, semantic entropy, derived from clustering generated answers by meaning, demonstrates potential for improving accuracy by allowing uncertain queries to be routed to larger expert models, achieving improvements of up to +50 percentage points in accuracy.

 - Token-level entropy is largely ineffective in Small Language Models.
 - Semantic entropy can significantly improve accuracy by better directing uncertain queries to expert models.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20824

 - Entropy-based confidence signals can improve the accuracy of small language models.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20824
